Engineering Case Study — 04

Teaching CCTV cameras to catch traffic violations

TypeAcademic / research project
TimelineJan 2026 — May 2026
RoleML developer
StackPython · OpenCV · Machine Learning
Result~90% precision, up from 72%
The Problem

Cameras everywhere, and a human watching every one.

Traffic enforcement via CCTV depends on manual monitoring — slow, expensive and inconsistent. Two violation types are both common and visually detectable: red-light violations and riding without a helmet. The goal: detect them automatically from raw footage.

The Solution

A vision pipeline, improved iteration by iteration.

I built a computer-vision pipeline in Python and OpenCV: frames are preprocessed, passed through object detection, and classified against violation rules. The first working version reached 72% precision — the interesting engineering was everything after that.

Systematic iteration on image preprocessing and the detection pipeline — evaluated against a fixed 500-image dataset — lifted precision to approximately 90%.

Challenges & Trade-offs
Challenge 01

Where did 18 points of precision come from?

Not from swapping models — from disciplined evaluation. A fixed 500-image dataset made every preprocessing and pipeline change measurable, so improvements compounded instead of guessing which tweak helped.

Challenge 02

Real CCTV footage is nothing like clean datasets

Variable lighting, weather, occlusion and low resolution break naive detection. The preprocessing stage carried real weight — normalizing frames before detection was worth more than tuning the detector itself.

Impact
~90%Detection precision
72% → 90%Precision gain
500Image evaluation dataset
Lessons Learned
In ML work, the evaluation setup is the product. Once changes became measurable, improving the system became engineering instead of alchemy. — Measure first, then optimize
